title: Counting journeys
bodyMd:
A fictional distributor replaced disposable produce boxes with reusable crates. Its first report compared the materials needed to manufacture one crate with those needed for one disposable box, making the crate look wasteful. An employee objected that a crate was designed for many journeys. A later calculation spread manufacturing impacts over the number of uses actually achieved and included washing and return transport.

The new calculation did not produce a single answer independent of operations. Crates returned promptly and reused many times performed differently from crates lost after two deliveries or transported empty over long distances. The distributor began tracking losses and return routes alongside purchase numbers. The environmental question had become a question about a system of use, not simply a contest between two objects sitting unused on a table.
